dispositions.title: Privileged mintFor()/burn() ignore paused + per-index disabled flags
dispositions.fingerprintBasis: src/V2/NFTMinterV2.sol:mintFor/burn:incomplete pause/disabled enforcement on privileged supply-changing entry points
dispositions.rationale: NOT suppressed by KI-5 (pauser trust) or KI-4 (owner trust): those KIs trust the pauser/owner as ACTORS, they do not bless an incomplete kill-switch MECHANISM. The pause-bypass is deliberate-by-design (reverted story-033 justified a pause-exempt migration primitive) so that leg is faithful; but the DISABLED-bypass is a Law-2 spec deviation (no story authorizes ignoring config.disabled, contradicts documented 'new mints blocked' semantics) AND a non-obvious owner footgun (owner who disables an index would be surprised the migrator path still mints it). Survives at honest Low; mints are 1:1 vs burned V1, no net inflation, only the trusted minter benefits.

dispositions.title: Gross mint-debt vs exported-donation under-backs phUSD when batchDonationSize + ratio > 100
dispositions.rationale: SPLIT call. (a) SUPPRESSED part: the 'phUSD is unbacked / value can leak from the backing model' SECURITY claim is a duplicate of hard-suppressed DEDUP-001 - econ REFUTE-A proves the retained-collateral/minted ratio is ARITHMETICALLY UNCHANGED from the pre-story-034 baseline; story-034 changed donation MECHANISM (AMM swap -> fixed-rate PSM) and timing, not the backing arithmetic. The external phUSD backing layer is OOS (KI-1/KI-4). This claim is NOT re-litigated as a fresh unbacked-phUSD finding; it is parked visibly here. (b) SURVIVES part: story-034 introduced a NEW donation->PSM-export mechanism and the Tier-3 invariant pins a concrete, in-protocol, owner-actionable guardrail (batchDonationSize + ratio <= 100) that did NOT exist when DEDUP-001 was suppressed. The hazard that survives is strictly the un-coupled cross-contract parameter design: two owner setters in two separate contracts (BalancerPoolerV2.batchDonationSize cap 100, Hook.ratio cap 50) with NO on-chain linking invariant, so an owner can silently cross the solvency boundary. That is a genuinely non-obvious footgun (Law 3 in-scope), not a re-assertion that the backing model is broken. Carry it as a fresh Low/QA operational-footgun carrying the proven guardrail. NO permissionless trigger (invariant-confirmed).
dispositions.scopeGuard: The surviving finding MUST be framed as the unlinked-knobs / missing on-chain invariant operator guardrail (documentation/ops hazard) and MUST NOT be written as a fresh 'phUSD unbacked' security claim - that framing is DEDUP-001 and stays suppressed.

dispositions.title: pool() single-sided sUSDS LP-add relies solely on keeper minBPT, no on-chain price reference (MEV)
dispositions.fingerprintBasis: src/V2/dispatchers/BalancerPoolerV2.sol:pool:missing on-chain slippage reference / off-chain-trusted bound (MEV LP-add sandwich)
dispositions.rationale: DISTINCT from the FIXED L-03 and therefore NOT a regression. L-03 was the OLD donation sUSDS->waUSDC AMM swap (limitRaw=0 / pooler minUSDC floor) eliminated wholesale by story-034 (root cause genuinely removed). DD-04 is the SEPARATE pooling leg: the single-sided AddLiquidityKind.UNBALANCED join whose only protection is an off-chain keeper-supplied minBPT - a surface never adjudicated. Same contract+function name ('pool') as L-03 but a DIFFERENT rootCauseClass, so the fingerprint differs and there is no fixed-entry collision -> origin=new, not regression. The H-02 fix (accumulate-then-dump) AMPLIFIES price impact. Treasury value-leak bounded by keeper minBPT competence + permissioned trigger -> honest Low. Do NOT auto-suppress as 'already fixed'.

dispositions.title: replaceDispatcher() carries stale per-index price to a new dispatcher with a different primeToken (re-denomination)
dispositions.fingerprintBasis: src/V2/NFTMinterV2.sol:replaceDispatcher:config carry-over across dispatcher swap with different prime token (price-denomination mismatch)
dispositions.rationale: NON-OBVIOUS owner footgun, not an obvious misconfig (Law 3 in-scope). replaceDispatcher's name implies a like-for-like swap and gives no hint that price persists in NFTMinterV2 while its DENOMINATION is defined by whichever dispatcher is currently bound; swapping an 18-dp USDS dispatcher for a 6-dp token dispatcher silently mis-scales the carried-over price until setPrice is called. A competent non-malicious owner would be surprised -> footgun, keep. DISTINCT aspect from C-01: C-01 tracks the general re-pointing of token/metadata under existing holders; it does NOT cover the price re-denomination sub-issue. Survives as a fresh Low footgun; classifier may alternatively fold it as a new sub-item under the C-01 bundle. Flagged for human review on the C-01 boundary.
